<reason>A wins the actual comparison: enforceable reserve and liquidity supervision resembles financial-institution regulation more than ordinary software governance. A answered the demand for a concrete tool with a stressed-redemption liquidity requirement and consistently defended proportionality. B’s custody alternative initially created useful pressure, but B ultimately accepted a liquidity floor while insisting that A must import an entire bank/MMF template. That requirement does not follow from “more like,” and several supposedly abandoned policies were expressly excluded in A’s opening.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s distinction between full backing and immediate payability directly defeated B’s claim that safe assets and real-time reserve reporting suffice. Reporting cannot release inaccessible custodial funds or prevent a liquidity shortfall. B’s subsequent acceptance of enforceable liquid-reserve requirements substantially conceded the underlying need while leaving its objection largely about labels.</best_rebuttal>
